I will still do it close to last year, because on 8 mu I cannot gamble. My main land will stay in wheat-maize, because that is what feeds the house and brings steady money here. I will put 6 mu into winter wheat, then that same 6 mu goes into summer maize after wheat harvest. I will leave 2 mu for cotton, because cotton takes more watching and more spraying, and with some people working off-farm I do not want too much labor tied up there. I do what the better growers around me do: wheat and maize get the stronger fertilizer, because if those two miss yield, the loss is heavy. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than watch the field stay thin. For wheat, I will put more base fertilizer before sowing and then chase once in spring with water from the well. For maize, I will put fertilizer at sowing and then one more time when it grows fast. Cotton I will not plant too much, but I will feed it enough and spray it more times because bugs on cotton can spoil the whole thing fast. I will use improved or hybrid seed where I have seen it work on neighbors' fields, but I will not push the rates too hard because fertilizer, pesticide, and hired help all cost cash.
